title: Dead-End Fields (Write-Only Fields)
pattern: Fields on a struct that are assigned values during initialization or execution but are never read or queried anywhere in the codebase.
why_bad: Wastes memory, increases the struct size, and forces developers to maintain complex writes and synchronization logic for data that has no effect.
detection: Struct fields that are targets of assignment but never appear as r-values or references in reads.
counterexample: Fields used purely in test assertions (though even these are smell candidates; prefer behavioral tests).
fix: Delete the field, its initialization, and all associated write/assignment code.
source: Fowler, *Refactoring*, Chapter 3 ("Bad Smells - Dead Code"); Robert C. Martin, *Clean Code*, Chapter 17, G9.
